name: American Express
description: American Express is a global payments company offering personal, small-business, and corporate cards, merchant services, rewards, travel benefits, and selected banking products. Card Members use its digital account tools to review balances and activity, manage cards and statements, make payments, and access rewards and benefits.
agentUseSummary: American Express is visible as an Open Banking partner-review preview only. Relay will not collect an American Express User ID, password, one-time code, browser session, Card number, security code, PIN, or developer credential, and no agent action is callable until American Express onboards and approves Relay for an exact customer-authorized account-data product.

capabilities.label: Read approved Card account data
capabilities.description: After American Express onboards and approves Relay, expose only bounded non-mutating summaries for the connected Card Member's authorized Card accounts and recent transaction lifecycle within explicitly approved products and jurisdictions.

blocked.label: Connect before partner approval
blocked.description: American Express data sharing is available to onboarded financial-service providers, while its public Account and Transaction API is limited to parties certified under PSD2. Relay has no approved product, applicable certification, contract, customer-authorization model, scopes, credentials, sandbox acceptance, or production access.

blocked.label: Collect Card Member credentials
blocked.description: Relay will not ask Card Members for an American Express User ID, password, one-time code, browser session, bearer token, Card number, security code, PIN, account number, identity document, Social Security number, developer credential, or other secret as a substitute for American Express-hosted authorization.

blocked.label: Run American Express API actions
blocked.description: No account, balance, transaction, Card, statement, reward, benefit, offer, payment, transfer, identity, consent, webhook, or other American Express API action can run while partner, jurisdiction, product, and production review is pending.

blocked.label: Money movement unavailable
blocked.description: Payments, transfers, bill pay, Card controls, account maintenance, disputes, rewards redemption, offers, lending, and every other financial or account mutation remain outside Relay's planned read-only V1 even after approval.

approvalProfiles.label: Open Banking partner review pending
approvalProfiles.description: Agent actions remain unavailable until American Express approves Relay's exact account-data product, jurisdiction, customer-authorization contract, and production integration.

runtimeSupport.description: No OpenClaw tools are callable until American Express approves Relay and Relay implements the approved read-only Railway broker.
No Hermes tools are callable until American Express approves Relay and Relay implements the approved read-only Railway broker.

providerSetup.blocker: American Express documents customer-permissioned API data sharing for onboarded financial-service providers, including an American Express-hosted sign-in, account selection, and revocation. Its public Account and Transaction API is described for parties certified under PSD2, and the general developer journey may require product access, contracts, certificates, sandbox testing, and explicit production approval. Relay has no approved product or jurisdiction, applicable certification, signed contract, scopes, authorization and token contract, credentials, certificates, sandbox acceptance, schema and rate-limit contract, privacy allocation, or production authority, so no connection can be offered safely.
providerSetup.nextAction: An authorized Relay business, legal, compliance, privacy, and security owner must ask American Express to onboard Relay as a financial-service provider for the intended jurisdictions and obtain written product and production approval. The owner must document eligibility and certifications, exact Card products and read permissions, minimized response fields, American Express-hosted authorization copy and duration, authorization and token contracts, credentials and certificates, sandbox and production onboarding, schemas and rate limits, data retention, revocation and disconnect, audits, incident duties, and production approval. Engineering can then implement a fixed-origin Railway authorization broker and the smallest bounded read-only Card-account and recent transaction-lifecycle V1. Money movement and every mutation remain excluded.

evidence.supports: American Express describes its Account and Transaction API as customer-authorized, account-specific data for proprietary personal, small-business, and corporate Card products, limited to parties certified under PSD2.

The official integration journey may require outreach, contracts, a developer project, certificates and authentication information, sandbox testing, promotion, and full production approval before production credentials are issued.

American Express says only onboarded financial-service providers use its API flow; Card Members authenticate in an American Express-hosted window, choose accounts, and can revoke permission, while credential sharing is discouraged.

American Express describes Account Financials API access as a customer-permissioned agreement with a named data partner that avoids credential sharing, supporting a partner-contract rather than generic credential model.
